note: Every backend/src/**/*.ts arithmetic site this ratchet finds outside *.spec.ts/*.db-spec.ts, as of 2026-09-15: 29 keys, 32 occurrences. THE SCOPE WIDENED ON 2026-09-15 and the count did not move: until then this ratchet skipped the four module trees backend/eslint.config.mjs policed when it was written (src/intakes/, src/payouts/, src/shifts/, src/supplier-balance/). eslint's own `files` list had since grown to eight trees while this ratchet's hard-coded copy of it had not, so the two scopes silently disagreed — and a tree DELETED from eslint's list would have been policed by neither. Scanning all of backend/src was measured before the carve-out was removed: exactly zero additional findings, because eslint's ban is what keeps those trees clean. Read individually before writing a reason, not inferred from the shape of the code. Four of the 29 keys are backend/src/common/money.ts's OWN internals (the *, /, and mul()'s two / occurrences on one line) — the money engine works in bigint, not JS number, so it carries none of the float-precision risk this ratchet exists to catch, but the AST heuristic only recognises number-typed or numeric-literal operands, not bigint-safety, so those sites are listed honestly here rather than exempted by widening the rule's path exclusions. Three keys (backend/src/seed/dev-seed.ts:59 and :66) are a genuine concern, not a false positive: the dev seed script reimplements money.ts's add() independently, through Number() and plain-number division, to compute real values written into grade_prices.base_price for the seeded demo dataset — a real duplicate of the one authorised rounding seam, left as-is because backend/src is out of scope for the verify layer. Two keys (password-hashing.ts:28's two occurrences) are literal-and-number-typed arithmetic that this rule's single-level operand check cannot prove clear because each is the OUTER multiplication of a left-associative a*b*c chain, whose left operand is itself a BinaryExpression rather than a bare literal or identifier. Every remaining key is one of two shapes: the repeated (page - 1) * limit pagination-offset arithmetic this template's list endpoints all share (10 keys, including pagination-query.dto.ts's own skipOf() helper), or an env-var/config integer parsed with Number()/parseInt() (ports, throttle window/limit) or Math.min() retry-backoff arithmetic that is never a monetary or weight value. None were left unclassified — every entry's reason states what the arithmetic actually is, read at its site. Five entries were RE-KEYED on 2026-09-15 rather than added: all five are sites this file already carried, whose line numbers moved under main's merge. This ratchet is two-directional: a new site not listed here fails scripts/verify/ratchets/money-rounding.mjs, and a listed entry whose site (or exact occurrence count) no longer matches the tree fails it too — this file may only shrink or be re-dated by a reviewed change, never grow by drift.

money.ts's own parse(): BigInt(whole) * UNIT, scaling the integer part of a decimal string up to kopiykas. This is the one seam §5.1 authorises to take a numeric string apart; it works in bigint, not JS number, so it carries none of the float-precision risk this ratchet exists to catch — but the AST heuristic only recognises number-typed/numeric-literal operands, not bigint-safety, so it is listed honestly here rather than exempted by path.

money.ts's own format(): magnitude / UNIT, recovering the whole-kopiyka part from the internal bigint representation before rendering it back to a decimal string. Same seam, same bigint-not-number reasoning as line 43 above.

money.ts's own mul(): parse(a) * parse(b), the scale-4 bigint product before mul() rounds it back to scale 2 half-up. This IS the rounding engine itself — §2.7's amount calculation runs through exactly this line — audited by money.spec.ts, not by this AST heuristic.

money.ts's own mul(): (magnitude + UNIT / 2n) / UNIT implements half-up-away-from-zero rounding on the bigint product; the two / occurrences on this one line are the inner UNIT / 2n and the outer division by UNIT. Same seam as lines 43/51/75 — bigint arithmetic implementing the one authorised rounding rule, not a bypass of it.
parseInt(process.env.PORT ?? '3000', 10) — the HTTP listen port, an integer read from an env var; never a monetary or weight value.
parseInt(process.env.TRUST_PROXY_HOPS ?? '0', 10) — how many reverse-proxy hops to trust for client-IP resolution; a small integer count, not money.
parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT ?? '5432', 10) — the Postgres TCP port, an integer read from an env var; not money.
parseInt(process.env.REDIS_PORT ?? '6379', 10) — the Redis TCP port, an integer read from an env var; not money.

`((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296` — the final step of a seeded xorshift PRNG, normalising a 32-bit integer into [0, 1). Arithmetic on a bit pattern, with no monetary or weight value anywhere near it. Arrived with main's seeded history generator.

`lo + Math.floor(rand() * (hi - lo + 1))` — an integer-range picker over the PRNG above. Its CALLERS sometimes pick monetary amounts (see the :190 entry), but this expression itself only scales a [0,1) float into a count of discrete steps.

`Math.floor(abs / 100)` inside the module's own kopiyka-to-string formatter, beside an `abs % 100` for the fractional part. THIS IS REAL MONEY ARITHMETIC and a third independent reimplementation of what backend/src/common/money.ts exists to own — the same finding this baseline already records for dev-seed.ts:77, now duplicated in a second seed module. Recorded so it is visible, NOT endorsed: it is confined to the dev-only seed CLI, which never runs as part of the app, and backend/src is out of scope for the verify layer's own refactors.

`between(-10, 10) * 100` — generates a demo bonus line as a whole number of hryvni converted to kopiykas. Monetary, dev-seed only, same standing as the :116 entry: the figure is invented demo data, so no rule about rounding real money applies to it.

`Number(grade.base_price.slice(0, grade.base_price.indexOf('.')))` — takes the whole-hryvnia part of a `numeric` price string to derive a plausible demo payout rate. It DISCARDS the kopiyka part by construction, which is exactly the kind of silent precision loss money.ts exists to prevent — harmless only because the output is invented seed data and never an amount the app computed.

`grossCents * rate` in `Math.floor((grossCents * rate) / 100)` — accumulates what a demo supplier is owed, in kopiykas. Real money arithmetic outside money.ts, dev-seed only; see the :116 entry for the full standing of this module.

`(grossCents * rate) / 100` — the division half of the same accumulation, on the same line. Recorded separately because this ratchet keys by file:line:kind and the two operators are independently findable.
`Math.floor(owed[1] / 4 / 100) * 100` — pays a demo supplier roughly a quarter of what they are owed, rounded down to whole hryvni. Money arithmetic, dev-seed only, same standing as :116.

`owed[1] / 4 / 100` — TWO divisions on one line, which is why this entry's count is 2 where every other on this file is 1: the quarter-share and the kopiyka-to-hryvnia step are separate operators the scan finds separately. Money arithmetic, dev-seed only, same standing as :116.

maxmemFor()'s own body: Math.max(32 * 1024 * 1024, 256 * n * r) computes scrypt's maxmem option in bytes from the cost parameters N and r. Each inner multiplication (32 * 1024, 256 * n) clears on its own since every operand is a number-typed identifier or a numeric literal, but this rule inspects only a BinaryExpression's two immediate operands, so the OUTER multiplication in each left-associative chain ((32 * 1024) * 1024 and (256 * n) * r) sees a nested BinaryExpression as its left operand and is not provably cleared by this single-level heuristic. This is scrypt memory sizing, not money or weight.
const n = Number(rawN) — parses the scrypt cost parameter N back out of the self-describing stored-hash format (scrypt$N$r$p$salt$hash); a cost parameter, not money.
const r = Number(rawR) — same stored-hash format, the scrypt cost parameter r; not money.
const p = Number(rawP) — same stored-hash format, the scrypt cost parameter p; not money.
